current_measurements.naive_prewarm_rejected: An env-gated post-boot static graph prewarm prototype compiled only one block per DSP (DSP2 compiled=1, DSP1 compiled=1) and did not reduce live JIT counts. It was removed rather than committed as a false optimization; next work must determine whether repeated compiles are due mode chains, P-memory invalidation, or dynamic dispatch before proposing prewarm/defer.
current_measurements.hotpc_existing_chain_prewarm_rejected: A second env-gated prototype added Jit::prewarmExistingChains() and called it at DSP boot completion with 20 hot low-vector PCs. It compiled 20 blocks per DSP before BOOTTRACE but regressed mmAudioFirmwareTest RTJIT metrics: live compiles 403 -> 457, JIT windows 7/13 -> 9/13, max block ~28.85 ms bounded-trace baseline -> 36.275 ms. Code was reverted; do not revive simple hot-PC prewarm across existing chains.

active_hypotheses: Pure time-skip for the DSP2 CVR poll loop is unsafe: CVR reads must still invoke m_readCvrCallback so DSP catch-up and host-command acceptance timing remain real.

A full CVR loop accelerator is only viable if it batches taken iterations while still performing CVR reads and checking host-pump/deferred-RX/IRQ/timer/MIDI boundaries between MOVE and BLT. The single-MOVE fast path is rejected by measurement.

DSP2 heavier steady-state wall time is real work, but the large per-block spikes are now attributed to synchronous live DSP JIT compilation inside render callbacks; steady non-JIT windows still hover near the 5.805 ms budget and need separate DSP2 throughput work.

A simple first-PC/static-branch prewarm is insufficient: the trace shows dynamic/low-vector repeated compile events after boot. v23 classified the repeats: P-memory invalidation is not the main cause; the same PCs compile under multiple SR-mode JIT chains. v24 further shows naive hot-PC prewarm across existing chains regresses; a useful fix must avoid creating more wrong/soon-invalidated blocks and must target the actual live create path.
next_steps: If continuing UC work, prototype a full taken-iteration CVR loop batch with explicit post-CVR host boundary checks, not the rejected single-MOVE path.

If continuing DSP work, do not use simple boot-time hot-PC prewarm. Next viable direction is synchronous-create avoidance: detect create()/recreate() while inside realtime render, execute a bounded interpreter fallback for the cold block, and queue/compile outside the critical path only if an actual non-realtime maintenance point exists.
After JIT spikes are removed, target steady DSP2 throughput because dsp2 remains the largest total wall-time component (~149.55 ms/window vs uc ~113.18 ms and dsp1 ~98.34 ms in v21 profile).
Run host/VST3 smoke with Thor after any default-on perf change; headless probes alone are not host acceptance.
